extracted.intended_audience: federal agency standards program managers, OMB reviewers, and regulatory policy staff
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare an agency narrative and quantitative report to comply with OMB Circular A-119, addressing participation in voluntary consensus standards bodies, use and substitution of standards, evaluations of Circular A-119 policy effectiveness, and instances where government-unique standards were used instead of voluntary consensus standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of voluntary consensus standards bodies and agency employees participating
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of voluntary consensus standards bodies in which there is agency participation, as well as the number of agency employees participating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts (example: FDA: 46 bodies; 274 employees participating on 553 committees). Note that individual employees may participate on multiple committees simultaneously; clarify whether counts are bodies, distinct employee headcount, and committee memberships. Include specific organizations with which employees participate when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of voluntary consensus standards the agency has used since October 1, 1997
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of voluntary consensus standards the agency has used since October 1, 1997 based on the procedures set forth in sections 11 and 12 of the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numeric totals and note inclusions/exclusions (example: FDA included standards recognized under FDAMA). Where relevant, cite specific Orders or rule provisions that incorporated standards by reference (e.g., FERC Order Nos. 587 series). If standards are catalogued in a database, indicate how the count was derived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of voluntary consensus standards substituted for government-unique standards (section 15b(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of voluntary consensus standards that have been substituted for government-unique standards as a result of an agency review under section 15b(7) of the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State each instance (or '0' if none) and include the specific government-unique standard replaced and the agency rationale. Note special cases (FDA: certification to consensus standards can replace some data submission requirements for device premarket approval, even if not strictly substituting a government-unique standard).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of the effectiveness of Circular A-119 policy and recommendations for changes
rubrics_metrics.description: An evaluation of the effectiveness of Circular A-119 policy and recommendations for any changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a narrative assessment of how A-119 has worked for the agency, resource constraints, areas needing elaboration (e.g., forums agencies should use to increase awareness of standards), and specific recommendations. Include center- or program-specific evaluations (examples: FDA notes high relevance for medical devices and limited relevance for pharmaceuticals/food). Training plans and procedural improvements (e.g., planned training for regulation writers) are appropriate content for this evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of instances where government-unique standards were used instead of voluntary consensus standards (with rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by P.L. 104-113, identification of all instances when the agency used government-unique standards in lieu of voluntary consensus standards (for each instance include agency rationale for such use, as well as the specific government-unique standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List instances (or '0' if none) and provide detailed rationale explaining why a voluntary consensus standard was unsuitable. Include cross-references to statutory requirements or other policies that compelled use of government-unique standards. Provide counts and attach lists of the specific government-unique standards where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards-development body consensus/ratification thresholds (GISB example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural thresholds required by a standards body for a prospective standard to be accepted and ratified (GISB example: prospective standards must get at least 17 affirmative votes in the Executive Committee, at least two affirmative votes for each segment, and 67% affirmative vote of ballots for membership ratification; Board bylaw/article changes need at least 19 affirmative votes with at least two from each segment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the approval/voting rules of relevant voluntary consensus organizations that the agency relies on or references; include detail about segment-based voting, quorum/percentage thresholds, and accreditation status (e.g., GISB filed with ANSI). These thresholds are used to assess whether industry consensus exists for incorporation by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency practice for using standards (incorporation by reference vs. active participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the agency actively participates in consensus standards bodies or instead incorporates standards by reference in its regulations (FERC example: does not actively participate as specified in section 7 of the Circular; instead incorporates industry-adopted standards by reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the agency's approach to using voluntary consensus standards: active participation, reliance on industry-developed standards, incorporation by reference, or a hybrid. Provide examples of Orders/rules implementing standards (e.g., FERC adoption of GISB standards in Order Nos. 587, 587-B, 587-C, 587-H). Clarify when the agency will adopt standards only after industry segments concur and when the agency may step in where consensus fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for when to adopt or use voluntary consensus standards (FDA policy criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy criteria for adopting/using standards: agency adopts or uses standards when doing so will enhance its ability to protect consumers and the effectiveness or efficiency of regulatory efforts; to facilitate harmonization with foreign governments; to implement statutory provisions for safeguarding public health; and to respond to laws/policies encouraging use of voluntary standards that provide the desired degree of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how the agency evaluates relevance and applicability of standards to particular product areas (example: FDA finds voluntary standards most relevant to medical devices, less relevant for pharmaceuticals/biologics/food). Describe decision factors (public health protection, regulatory efficiency, availability of international standards) and reference enabling statutes or acts (e.g., FDAMA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program management structures and practices for standards activities (FDA SPC, databases, training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational and program-management mechanisms to manage standards activity: Standards Policy Committee (SPC) oversight, standards executive, liaison experts, searchable standards databases, tracking/reporting systems, and training plans for Circular A-119 compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe roles and responsibilities (SPC reviews/coordinates agency-wide standards policy, ensures appropriate standards review, tracks/reports required information). Note operational practices such as maintaining searchable ROM databases of standards, providing training for regulation writers and standards staff, and planning periodic recognition/updates of standards lists under statutory authorities (e.g., FDAMA recognition lists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in international and non-reportable standards forums and harmonization initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency participation in international standards and harmonization activities (e.g., ICH, WHO, OECD, VICH, Codex Alimentarius, PAHO, WTO TBT/SPS committees, APEC initiatives) that may be excluded from Circular A-119 reporting but are central to agency regulatory missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report engagement in treaty or multilateral organizations even if not reportable under Circular A-119; explain how these activities support regulatory objectives (e.g., harmonizing pharmaceutical testing guidelines via ICH, developing good laboratory practices via OECD). List planned participation (conferences, delegations) and how outputs are used in agency regulatory work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement to explain deviations from national consensus standards (OSHA Act §6 example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an agency rule differs substantially from an existing national consensus standard, the agency (OSHA example) must publish in the Federal Register a statement of reasons why the adopted rule will better effectuate statutory purposes than the national consensus standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite statutory or regulatory mandates that require explicit justification when agency rules deviate from consensus standards. Explain how this requirement influences agency involvement in consensus standards development and reporting (OSHA involvement in standards committees to be prepared to explain deviations).
